     3	/// Resolves comment anchors once against the concatenated per-chunk
     4	/// plain-text projection — the same corpora `MarkdownFindState` searches —
     5	/// then hands each chunk only the anchors whose resolved range overlaps it.
     6	///
     7	/// `HighlightingMarkdownParser.resolveRange` picks exactly one best match
     8	/// inside whatever string it is given. Feeding every chunk the full
     9	/// document-wide anchor list therefore paints a recurring `exact` once per
    10	/// section, and drops a selection that straddles a heading (it is in no
    11	/// chunk's text). Resolving against the concatenation first restores the
    12	/// pre-chunking "one span in the document" rule; a range that crosses a
    13	/// heading is clipped so each overlapping chunk highlights its piece.
    14	enum MarkdownCommentAnchorMap {
    15	    private struct Projection {
    16	        var plains: [String]
    17	        var starts: [Int]
    18	        var concat: String
    19	    }
    20	
    21	    struct ChunkAnchors: Equatable {
    22	        var highlighted: [CommentAnchor]
    23	        var flashing: CommentAnchor?
    24	
    25	        static let empty = ChunkAnchors(highlighted: [], flashing: nil)
    26	    }
    27	
    28	    /// Memoizes `partition` across SwiftUI `body` evaluations. Held as a
    29	    /// reference type so a cache hit does not write `@State`.
    30	    @MainActor
    31	    final class Cache {
    32	        private var source: String?
    33	        private var headings: Set<String>?
    34	        private var highlighted: [CommentAnchor]?
    35	        private var flashing: CommentAnchor?
    36	        private var baseURL: URL?
    37	        private var projection: Projection?
    38	        private var value: [ChunkAnchors] = []
    39	
    40	        func partition(
    41	            source: String,
    42	            headings: Set<String>,
    43	            chunks: [MarkdownDocumentChunk],
    44	            highlighted: [CommentAnchor],
    45	            flashing: CommentAnchor?,
    46	            baseURL: URL?
    47	        ) -> [ChunkAnchors] {
    48	            let projectionIsCurrent = self.source == source
    49	                && self.headings == headings
    50	                && self.baseURL == baseURL
    51	                && projection?.plains.count == chunks.count
    52	            if projectionIsCurrent,
    53	               self.highlighted == highlighted,
    54	               self.flashing == flashing {
    55	                return value
    56	            }
    57	            self.source = source
    58	            self.headings = headings
    59	            self.highlighted = highlighted
    60	            self.flashing = flashing
    61	            self.baseURL = baseURL
    62	            if !projectionIsCurrent {
    63	                projection = MarkdownCommentAnchorMap.projection(for: chunks, baseURL: baseURL)
    64	            }
    65	            value = MarkdownCommentAnchorMap.assign(
    66	                highlighted: highlighted,
    67	                flashing: flashing,
    68	                projection: projection!,
    69	            )
    70	            return value
    71	        }
    72	    }
    73	
    74	    /// Builds the concatenated per-chunk projection and assigns each
    75	    /// resolved range to the chunk(s) it overlaps. Anchors that miss the
    76	    /// projection entirely are dropped (same silent no-op as the parser).
    77	    @MainActor
    78	    static func partition(
    79	        chunks: [MarkdownDocumentChunk],
    80	        highlighted: [CommentAnchor],
    81	        flashing: CommentAnchor?,
    82	        baseURL: URL?
    83	    ) -> [ChunkAnchors] {
    84	        guard !chunks.isEmpty else { return [] }
    85	        return assign(
    86	            highlighted: highlighted,
    87	            flashing: flashing,
    88	            projection: projection(for: chunks, baseURL: baseURL)
    89	        )
    90	    }
    91	
    92	    @MainActor
    93	    private static func projection(for chunks: [MarkdownDocumentChunk], baseURL: URL?) -> Projection {
    94	        let plains = chunks.map { CommentProjection.plainText(for: $0.renderedText, baseURL: baseURL) }
    95	        var starts: [Int] = []
    96	        var cursor = 0
    97	        for plain in plains {
    98	            starts.append(cursor)
    99	            cursor += plain.count
   100	        }
   101	        return Projection(plains: plains, starts: starts, concat: plains.joined())
   102	    }
   103	
   104	    @MainActor
   105	    private static func assign(
   106	        highlighted: [CommentAnchor],
   107	        flashing: CommentAnchor?,
   108	        projection: Projection
   109	    ) -> [ChunkAnchors] {
   110	        guard !highlighted.isEmpty || flashing != nil else {
   111	            return Array(repeating: .empty, count: projection.plains.count)
   112	        }
   113	
   114	        var result = Array(repeating: ChunkAnchors.empty, count: projection.plains.count)
   115	        for anchor in highlighted {
   116	            assign(anchor, in: projection.concat, plains: projection.plains, starts: projection.starts, to: &result, flashing: false)
   117	        }
   118	        if let flashing {
   119	            assign(flashing, in: projection.concat, plains: projection.plains, starts: projection.starts, to: &result, flashing: true)
   120	        }
   121	        return result
   122	    }
   123	
   124	    @MainActor
   125	    private static func assign(
   126	        _ anchor: CommentAnchor,
   127	        in concat: String,
   128	        plains: [String],
   129	        starts: [Int],
   130	        to result: inout [ChunkAnchors],
   131	        flashing: Bool
   132	    ) {
   133	        guard let resolved = HighlightingMarkdownParser.resolveRange(for: anchor, in: concat) else { return }
   134	        let match = characterOffsets(of: resolved, in: concat)
   135	        for index in plains.indices {
   136	            let chunkStart = starts[index]
   137	            let chunkEnd = chunkStart + plains[index].count
   138	            let overlapStart = max(match.lowerBound, chunkStart)
   139	            let overlapEnd = min(match.upperBound, chunkEnd)
   140	            guard overlapStart < overlapEnd else { continue }
   141	            let local = (overlapStart - chunkStart)..<(overlapEnd - chunkStart)
   142	            let clipped = clip(plains[index], to: local)
   143	            guard isAnchorable(clipped) else { continue }
   144	            if flashing {
   145	                result[index].flashing = clipped
   146	            } else {
   147	                result[index].highlighted.append(clipped)
   148	            }
   149	        }
   150	    }
   151	
   152	    /// Rewrites `exact`/`prefix`/`suffix` into the chunk's own projection so
   153	    /// the per-chunk parser can re-apply the highlight locally, including
   154	    /// when only a slice of a heading-straddling selection lives here.
   155	    private static func clip(_ plain: String, to local: Range<Int>) -> CommentAnchor {
   156	        let exact = substring(plain, local)
   157	        let prefixStart = max(0, local.lowerBound - 64)
   158	        let suffixEnd = min(plain.count, local.upperBound + 64)
   159	        let prefix = substring(plain, prefixStart..<local.lowerBound)
   160	        let suffix = substring(plain, local.upperBound..<suffixEnd)
   161	        return CommentAnchor(exact: exact, prefix: prefix, suffix: suffix)
   162	    }
   163	
   164	    static func isAnchorable(_ anchor: CommentAnchor) -> Bool {
   165	        !anchor.exact.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines).isEmpty
   166	    }
   167	
   168	    private static func characterOffsets(of range: Range<String.Index>, in string: String) -> Range<Int> {
   169	        let lower = string.distance(from: string.startIndex, to: range.lowerBound)
   170	        let upper = string.distance(from: string.startIndex, to: range.upperBound)
   171	        return lower..<upper
   172	    }
   173	
   174	    private static func substring(_ string: String, _ range: Range<Int>) -> String {
   175	        let start = string.index(string.startIndex, offsetBy: range.lowerBound)
   176	        let end = string.index(string.startIndex, offsetBy: range.upperBound)
   177	        return String(string[start..<end])
   178	    }
   179	}

     9	/// Selects how wide the document scroll column clamps to. Prose-only
    10	/// documents keep today's centered reading column (`readable`); documents
    11	/// containing a table widen the column (`wide`) so the table can use the
    12	/// freed-up margin space, while `BossMarkdownStyle`'s per-block prose clamp
    13	/// (not this container) is what keeps paragraphs at the readable measure
    14	/// inside the wider column. A pure function of the source text — no view
    15	/// state, no layout feedback — so widening never triggers a relayout loop.
    16	enum MarkdownDocumentMeasure {
    17	    /// The outer bound on the *padded* document column (see
    18	    /// `MarkdownDocumentColumn.body`, `MarkdownDocumentLayout.horizontalPadding`)
    19	    /// in a prose-only document. The actual glyph-rendering width is
    20	    /// `proseContent`, this value minus the 80pt of horizontal padding, not
    21	    /// this raw constant — see `proseContent` for the per-character math.
    22	    static let readable: CGFloat = 720
    23	    /// The document column width once a table is present.
    24	    static let wide: CGFloat = 1440
    25	    /// The actual glyph-rendering width prose gets: `readable` minus the
    26	    /// padding that sits inside the outer `.frame(maxWidth:)`. Matched by
    27	    /// `BossMarkdownStyle`'s per-block clamp so paragraphs stay this width
    28	    /// even inside `wide` documents, where the outer column widens for a
    29	    /// table and `readable` itself would no longer bound anything. This,
    30	    /// not `readable`, is what must be passed to the per-block prose clamp
    31	    /// (`markdownProseMeasure`) and to the header/divider frames, since
    32	    /// those bound content directly rather than a padded column. Measured
    33	    /// against the sans editorial body (`MarkdownEditorialMetrics.bodyScale`
    34	    /// × the 17pt system body, i.e. 19.04pt) with `NSAttributedString.size()`
    35	    /// over real technical-prose sentences: ~8.64pt/character, so the padded
    36	    /// column yields about 74 characters per line, at the top of the 65-75
    37	    /// reading-measure target.
    38	    static let proseContent: CGFloat = readable - 2 * MarkdownDocumentLayout.horizontalPadding
    39	
    40	    static func forSource(_ source: String) -> CGFloat {
    41	        containsTable(source) ? wide : readable
    42	    }
    43	
    44	    /// Detects a GitHub-flavored Markdown table via its delimiter row (e.g.
    45	    /// `| --- | --- |` or the equally legal `|-|-|`), not a bare `|`, since
    46	    /// prose and inline code routinely contain pipes without forming a
    47	    /// table. Skips fenced code blocks, since docs that show table syntax as
    48	    /// an example (this repo's own docs included) shouldn't widen the
    49	    /// column for it.
    50	    static func containsTable(_ source: String) -> Bool {
    51	        var previousRow: String? = nil
    52	        var inFencedCode = false
    53	        for line in source.components(separatedBy: "\n") {
    54	            if isFenceDelimiter(line) {
    55	                inFencedCode.toggle()
    56	                previousRow = nil
    57	                continue
    58	            }
    59	            guard !inFencedCode else { continue }
    60	            if let previousRow, isTableDelimiterRow(line, precedingRow: previousRow) {
    61	                return true
    62	            }
    63	            previousRow = line
    64	        }
    65	        return false
    66	    }
    67	
    68	    /// Not `private`: `MarkdownHeadingSections.headingLines` (below) reuses
    69	    /// this exact fence toggle so a `# comment` line inside a fenced code
    70	    /// block isn't mistaken for a heading/section boundary either.
    71	    static func isFenceDelimiter<S: StringProtocol>(_ line: S) -> Bool {
    72	        let trimmed = line.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces)
    73	        return trimmed.hasPrefix("```") || trimmed.hasPrefix("~~~")
    74	    }
    75	
    76	    /// A delimiter row is only a *table* delimiter row when it is pipe-
    77	    /// delimited and the row above it is a real, also pipe-delimited
    78	    /// content row with a matching cell count — that's what actually
    79	    /// distinguishes it from a thematic break (`---` alone on its own line)
    80	    /// or a setext heading underline (`Heading\n---`), neither of which
    81	    /// contains a `|`.
    82	    private static func isTableDelimiterRow(_ line: String, precedingRow: String) -> Bool {
    83	        let trimmed = line.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces)
    84	        guard trimmed.contains("-"), trimmed.contains("|") else { return false }
    85	        let cells = trimmed
    86	            .trimmingCharacters(in: CharacterSet(charactersIn: "|"))
    87	            .components(separatedBy: "|")
    88	        guard !cells.isEmpty else { return false }
    89	        guard
    90	            cells.allSatisfy({ cell in
    91	                cell.range(of: #"^\s*:?-+:?\s*$"#, options: .regularExpression) != nil
    92	            })
    93	        else { return false }
    94	
    95	        let precedingTrimmed = precedingRow.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces)
    96	        guard !precedingTrimmed.isEmpty, precedingTrimmed.contains("|") else { return false }
    97	        let precedingCells = precedingTrimmed
    98	            .trimmingCharacters(in: CharacterSet(charactersIn: "|"))
    99	            .components(separatedBy: "|")
   100	        return precedingCells.count == cells.count
   101	    }
   102	}

   115	/// background), and the Designs-tab reader (GitHub string, no find, no
   116	/// background). Opening the same document two ways produced visibly different

   120	///   applied to the scrolling document column so a comment sidebar / questions

   122	///   layering from the original disk viewer).

   670	/// Splits a markdown source into one `MarkdownDocumentChunk` per heading
   671	/// so each section can be its own `StructuredText` (bounding layout
   672	/// recursion and making `LazyVStack` effective). Headings whose exact text
   673	/// (level markers and surrounding whitespace stripped) appears in
   674	/// `collapsibleHeadings` become `.collapsible`; every other heading stays
   675	/// `.plain` and includes its heading line. A pure function over `String` —
   676	/// no Textual/StructuredText involvement — because Textual's block rendering
   677	/// has no supported hook for grouping or hiding a run of blocks (see the
   678	/// `HeadingStyle`/`BlockStyleConfiguration` types in `BossMarkdownStyle.swift`:
   679	/// each block is styled in isolation, with no source range or sibling
   680	/// awareness). Splitting the *source text* before it ever reaches
   681	/// `StructuredText`, and rendering each collapsible chunk as its own
   682	/// independently-parsed `StructuredText` behind a native SwiftUI disclosure
   683	/// control, is the same shape `TranscriptView` already uses for its
   684	/// per-segment `DisclosureGroup`s.
   685	enum MarkdownHeadingSections {
   686	    /// A matched section spans from its heading's own line through the line
   687	    /// immediately before the NEXT heading of *any* level — not the next
   688	    /// heading of the *same* level. A revision brief's per-finding headings
   689	    /// render as `### [severity] ...` directly after the boilerplate's `##
   690	    /// HARD RULE ...` heading with no intervening heading in between; a
   691	    /// same-level rule would treat those (deeper) finding headings as
   692	    /// children of the H2 and fold them along with it — exactly the
   693	    /// "findings must never collapse" outcome this function exists to
   694	    /// avoid. Any-level is also simpler to reason about: "this heading's
   695	    /// own prose, stopping at the very next heading" needs no notion of
   696	    /// outline nesting at all.
   697	    static func chunks(in source: String, collapsibleHeadings: Set<String>) -> [MarkdownDocumentChunk] {
   698	        let headings = headingLines(in: source)
   699	        guard !headings.isEmpty else { return [.plain(source)] }
   700	
   701	        var chunks: [MarkdownDocumentChunk] = []
   702	        var cursor = source.startIndex
   703	        for (i, heading) in headings.enumerated() {
   704	            if heading.lineRange.lowerBound > cursor {
   705	                chunks.append(.plain(String(source[cursor..<heading.lineRange.lowerBound])))
   706	            }
   707	            let sectionEnd = (i + 1 < headings.count) ? headings[i + 1].lineRange.lowerBound : source.endIndex

   709	                let body = String(source[heading.lineRange.upperBound..<sectionEnd])
   710	                chunks.append(.collapsible(heading: heading.text, body: body))
   711	            } else {
   712	                chunks.append(.plain(String(source[heading.lineRange.lowerBound..<sectionEnd])))
   713	            }
   714	            cursor = sectionEnd
   715	        }
   716	        if cursor < source.endIndex {
   717	            chunks.append(.plain(String(source[cursor...])))
   718	        }
   719	        return chunks
   720	    }

   722	    private struct HeadingLine {
   723	        let text: String
   724	        /// Spans the heading's own line, INCLUDING its trailing newline (or
   725	        /// through end-of-source if the heading is the last line) — so a
   726	        /// section's body starts exactly at `lineRange.upperBound`.
   727	        let lineRange: Range<String.Index>

   730	    /// Skips fenced code blocks via the same fence toggle
   731	    /// `MarkdownDocumentMeasure.containsTable` uses, so a `# comment` line
   732	    /// inside a ``` fence isn't mistaken for a heading/section boundary —
   733	    /// which would otherwise silently truncate a folded section and leave
   734	    /// the remainder of its body rendered unfolded.
   735	    private static func headingLines(in source: String) -> [HeadingLine] {
   736	        var results: [HeadingLine] = []
   737	        var lineStart = source.startIndex
   738	        var inFencedCode = false
   739	        while lineStart < source.endIndex {
   740	            let newline = source[lineStart...].firstIndex(of: "\n")
   741	            let contentEnd = newline ?? source.endIndex
   742	            let lineEnd = newline.map(source.index(after:)) ?? source.endIndex
   743	            let line = source[lineStart..<contentEnd]
   744	            if MarkdownDocumentMeasure.isFenceDelimiter(line) {
   745	                inFencedCode.toggle()
   746	            } else if !inFencedCode, let text = headingText(in: line) {
   747	                results.append(HeadingLine(text: text, lineRange: lineStart..<lineEnd))
   748	            }
   749	            lineStart = lineEnd
   750	        }
   751	        return results
   752	    }

   754	    /// A markdown ATX heading (`^ {0,3}#{1,6}[ \t]+...`) — CommonMark permits
   755	    /// up to three leading spaces before the `#` markers, so an indented
   756	    /// heading is still recognized; returns its trimmed text with the
   757	    /// leading whitespace and `#` markers stripped, or `nil` if `line` isn't
   758	    /// a heading.
   759	    private static func headingText(in line: Substring) -> String? {
   760	        var index = line.startIndex
   761	        var leadingSpaces = 0
   762	        while index < line.endIndex, line[index] == " ", leadingSpaces < 3 {
   763	            leadingSpaces += 1
   764	            index = line.index(after: index)
   765	        }
   766	        var level = 0
   767	        while index < line.endIndex, line[index] == "#" {
   768	            level += 1
   769	            index = line.index(after: index)
   770	        }
   771	        guard level >= 1, level <= 6, index < line.endIndex, line[index] == " " || line[index] == "\t" else {
   772	            return nil
   773	        }
   774	        let text = line[index...].trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces)
   775	        return text.isEmpty ? nil : text
   776	    }

   855	/// A heading-delimited section of a markdown document that folds behind a
   856	/// disclosure affordance. Used only where a caller explicitly opts a
   857	/// heading in via `MarkdownDocumentChrome.collapsedByDefaultHeadings`. The
   858	/// heading text always renders as the summary label — so the section is
   859	/// never invisible, and the collapsed state always names what's hidden
   860	/// (never a bare triangle) — but deliberately at quiet, near-body
   861	/// prominence rather than the source's real H2 size/weight: this is a
   862	/// disclosure control the reader is meant to skip, not a section title
   863	/// competing with the `###` findings nested beneath it. Styling it off the
   864	/// heading level it happens to be built from (rather than shrinking H2s in
   865	/// general) is the point — ordinary document H2s stay at full size.
   866	private struct CollapsibleMarkdownSection: View {
   867	    let heading: String
   868	    let sectionBody: String
   869	    let parser: any MarkupParser
   870	    var highlightGeneration: Int = 0
   871	    @Binding var isExpanded: Bool
   872	    @Environment(\.markdownEditorialStyle) private var isEditorial
   873	    @ScaledMetric(relativeTo: .body) private var bodySize: CGFloat = BossHeadingStyle.bodyPointSize
   874	
   875	    private var hiddenLineCount: Int {
   876	        max(sectionBody.split(separator: "\n", omittingEmptySubsequences: true).count, 1)
   877	    }
   878	
   879	    var body: some View {
   880	        VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 8) {
   881	            toggleButton
   882	            Rectangle()
   883	                .fill(BossMarkdownPalette.hairline)
   884	                .frame(height: 1)
   885	            if isExpanded {
   886	                DocumentStructuredText(
   887	                    text: sectionBody,
   888	                    parser: parser,
   889	                    highlightGeneration: highlightGeneration,
   890	                    chunkIndex: -1
   891	                )
   892	            }
   893	        }
   894	        .padding(.top, headingSpacing.top)
   895	        .padding(.bottom, headingSpacing.bottom)
   896	    }
   897	
   898	    private var toggleButton: some View {
   899	        Button {
   900	            isExpanded.toggle()
   901	        } label: {
   902	            HStack(alignment: .firstTextBaseline, spacing: 8) {
   903	                Image(systemName: isExpanded ? "chevron.down" : "chevron.right")
   904	                    .font(.callout.weight(.semibold))
   905	                    .foregroundStyle(BossMarkdownPalette.muted)
   906	                headingLabel
   907	                Spacer(minLength: 8)
   908	                Text(isExpanded ? "Collapse" : "Collapsed — \(hiddenLineCount) lines hidden. Click to expand.")
   909	                    .font(.caption)
   910	                    .foregroundStyle(BossMarkdownPalette.muted)
   911	            }
   912	            .contentShape(Rectangle())
   913	        }
   914	        .buttonStyle(.plain)
   915	        .accessibilityIdentifier("markdown-collapsible-section-toggle")
   916	        .accessibilityLabel(
   917	            isExpanded
   918	                ? "Collapse \(heading)"
   919	                : "Expand \(heading) — \(hiddenLineCount) lines hidden"
   920	        )
   921	    }

   923	    @ViewBuilder
   924	    private var headingLabel: some View {
   925	        // Same fixed body-size tracking in both editorial and compact mode —
   926	        // unlike a real heading, this control doesn't scale with document
   927	        // typography, so it needs no `EditorialHeadingTracking` derivation.
   928	        Text(heading)
   929	            .font(.system(size: headingPointSize, weight: headingWeight))
   930	            .foregroundStyle(BossMarkdownPalette.ink)
   931	            .tracking(-0.3)
   932	    }
   933	
   934	    /// Fixed at body size regardless of editorial/compact mode or the
   935	    /// source heading's level — a disclosure control reads as skippable
   936	    /// exactly because it does NOT scale up with document heading size.
   937	    private var headingPointSize: CGFloat {
   938	        BossHeadingStyle.bodyPointSize
   939	    }

   941	    /// Semibold (not the heavier editorial H1/H2 weight) is enough to read
   942	    /// as an interactive control label without competing with real headings.
   943	    private var headingWeight: Font.Weight {
   944	        .semibold
   945	    }
   946	
   947	    private var headingSpacing: (top: CGFloat, bottom: CGFloat) {
   948	        guard isEditorial else {
   949	            return (
   950	                top: BossHeadingStyle.headingBlockSpacingTop,
   951	                bottom: BossHeadingStyle.headingBlockSpacingBottom
   952	            )
   953	        }

   955	            top: bodySize * MarkdownEditorialMetrics.disclosureControlSpacing.top,
   956	            bottom: bodySize * MarkdownEditorialMetrics.disclosureControlSpacing.bottom
   957	        )
   958	    }

item.text:
PR [#2890](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/pull/2890) changes the markdown viewer’s unit of rendering from an entire document to individual heading sections. The main review path is **section splitting → lazy view hierarchy → cache invalidation → highlight refresh and anchor mapping**.

This guide compares `6f8ca351` with `12c538d6`.

**1. The problem being solved**

Most documents previously rendered through one `StructuredText`. Heading splitting existed, but only for explicitly collapsible sections. With the normal empty configuration, the splitter immediately returned the entire source:

```swift
guard !collapsibleHeadings.isEmpty else { return [.plain(source)] }
```

That content lived inside ordinary `VStack`s. Consequently, a long document’s off-screen sections remained part of the same eagerly laid-out markdown tree.

Highlight updates added another source of work: changing comments, flashing an anchor, or navigating find results incremented `parseVersion`, which supplied `.id(parseVersion)` on the document body. This forced recreation of its rendered subtree. Comment updates compensated by capturing the scroll offset and restoring it asynchronously after the remount.

The PR addresses both costs: the size of the layout tree SwiftUI needs immediately, and unnecessary reconstruction during subsequent updates.

**2. The core implementation, with a worked example**

The fix has three cooperating parts:

- Split ordinary documents at every recognized heading.
- Present those sections as separate children of a `LazyVStack` directly inside the `ScrollView`.
- Preserve the sections and their view identities across ordinary invalidations and highlight changes.

The decisive layout structure is in [MarkdownDocumentChrome.swift, line 327](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/MarkdownDocumentChrome.swift#L327). Abbreviating the styling and geometry modifiers:

```swift
ScrollView {
    LazyVStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 0) {
        header
        Divider()
        if let loadError {
            loadErrorView(loadError)
        }
        ForEach(loadError == nil ? renderedChunks : []) { entry in
            chunkView(entry)
                .bossMarkdown()
        }
    }
}
```

Both levels matter. A lazy stack cannot defer sections if the entire document is still one child. Conversely, splitting the source would not make an ordinary stack lazy.

For a concrete example, use the actual `largeHeadedDocument(sections: 24)` test fixture. It contains:

- `# Large document`, followed by an introductory paragraph.
- Twenty-four `## Section N` headings.
- A paragraph, nested list, and fenced Swift block in each section.

The lazy-layout test supplies this source with `commentsEnabled: false`, the default empty collapsible-heading set, and a **760 × 400** viewport.

| Step | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Split source | Empty collapsible set returns one `.plain(source)`. | Recognizes the title plus 24 section headings, producing **25 plain chunks**. |
| Construct renderers | One `StructuredText` contains the whole document. | Each chunk has its own `DocumentStructuredText`. |
| Lay out the initial viewport | The eager hierarchy reaches the whole markdown document. | The lazy hierarchy can defer distant sections. |
| Reevaluate the view with unchanged source/configuration | Recomputes the rendering inputs; the document remains one large layout unit. | Reuses cached chunks and document width; instantiated sections remain independent layout units. |

The observable regression check is deliberately structural, not a stopwatch benchmark: the new appearance probe must record **at least one and at most 12 of the 25 chunks** during the test’s observation window. The code does not specify an exact number of initially instantiated sections.

A useful boundary: a document with **no recognized ATX headings** still becomes one chunk. This optimization therefore depends on heading boundaries; it does not subdivide an exceptionally long heading-free document.

**3. Major logic and architecture changes**

Start with [the splitter, line 696](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/MarkdownDocumentChrome.swift#L696). It now iterates over **all** headings instead of just headings named in `collapsibleHeadings`:

```swift
let sectionEnd = (i + 1 < headings.count)
    ? headings[i + 1].lineRange.lowerBound
    : source.endIndex

if collapsibleHeadings.contains(heading.text) {
    let body = String(source[heading.lineRange.upperBound..<sectionEnd])
    chunks.append(.collapsible(heading: heading.text, body: body))
} else {
    chunks.append(.plain(String(source[heading.lineRange.lowerBound..<sectionEnd])))
}
```

Ordinary chunks retain their heading line. Collapsible chunks still render the heading separately as a disclosure label and send only the body through the markdown parser. Leading text before the first heading remains its own chunk. Sections end at the next heading of **any level**; fence-aware heading detection is retained.

Next, inspect the view hierarchy. The `ForEach` stays directly inside the lazy stack, and `.bossMarkdown()` moves onto each chunk. This matters because that modifier creates a `BossMarkdownTheme` wrapper: wrapping the entire collection would conceal the individual rows behind one child.

Spacing is now explicit. The header and divider receive 12-point bottom padding; subsequent plain chunks receive heading top spacing through `MarkdownChunkTopSpacing`. Geometry reporting also moves onto individual chunks. `StructuredTextHeightKey` reduces with `max`, so any positive chunk height can trigger the existing timing logs. Those logs now indicate initial chunk layout, not completion of layout for every section.

The next stop is [chunk caching, line 549](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/MarkdownDocumentChrome.swift#L549). `documentChunks` reuses cached chunks when source and collapsible-heading configuration match. Appearance and changes to either input refresh the cache, including the table-dependent document width. Before the cache is populated—or when its inputs differ—the getter computes the correct split directly.

Parser configurations are still assembled for every chunk. Also, plain-text projections still process the document when their caches are built. **The improvement is deferred rendering/layout and reuse of derived data; it does not eliminate all whole-document processing.**

Highlight refresh is handled by [DocumentStructuredText and MarkdownHighlightRefreshParser, line 778](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/MarkdownDocumentChrome.swift#L778):

```swift
StructuredText(
    MarkdownHighlightRefreshParser.tagged(text, generation: highlightGeneration),
    parser: MarkdownHighlightRefreshParser(inner: parser)
)
```

The generation changes the markup string by appending a trailing marker such as:

```text
\n\n<!--boss-md-refresh:7-->
```

The wrapper strips that marker before calling the actual parser. This uses `StructuredText`’s markup-change refresh path while retaining SwiftUI identity. It also keeps comment/search offsets based on the real text.

Accordingly, `.id(parseVersion)`, the scroll-offset preservation helper, and `MarkdownScrollController.currentOffset`/`restoreOffset` disappear. Find navigation still deliberately scrolls to its approximate target and expands a collapsed section containing the current match.

Finally, review the new [MarkdownCommentAnchorMap.swift](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Sources/Comments/MarkdownCommentAnchorMap.swift#L13). More rendering chunks introduce a correctness problem: passing every document anchor to every parser could highlight repeated text once per section, while a quote spanning sections would exist in no individual parser’s input.

The new mapping:

1. Projects each chunk into rendered plain text and concatenates those projections.
2. Resolves each anchor once globally using the existing context-sensitive resolver.
3. Intersects that range with each chunk.
4. Creates local anchors with clipped text and up to 64 characters of surrounding context.

The overlap calculation is:

```swift
let overlapStart = max(match.lowerBound, chunkStart)
let overlapEnd = min(match.upperBound, chunkEnd)
guard overlapStart < overlapEnd else { continue }
```

Whitespace-only fragments are discarded before reaching the local highlighter.

Its cache separates **projection validity** from **anchor assignment validity**. Source, heading configuration, base URL, and chunk count determine whether the projection can be reused. Changing highlighted or flashing anchors recomputes assignments against that existing projection.

`MarkdownFindState.swift` itself has only documentation changes. Its existing per-chunk search machinery automatically adopts the expanded splitting behavior through the shared helper.

**4. Tests added and supporting infrastructure**

All test changes are in [MarkdownDocumentChromeTests.swift](https://github.com/spinyfin/mono/blob/12c538d6f328d9f4cbb62c0ef69d6fa9b301500a/tools/boss/app-macos/Tests/BossTests/MarkdownDocumentChromeTests.swift#L289).

| Coverage | What the assertions establish |
|---|---|
| Updated splitting tests | Empty or nonmatching collapsible-heading sets still split real headings; ordinary chunks reconstruct the source exactly. |
| Heading-free boundary | Plain prose remains one unchanged chunk. |
| Updated fenced-code test | A `#` line inside a fence does not create a section; real headings still do. |
| Refresh marker | Generation zero leaves source unchanged; a nonzero tag changes the string and strips back to the original. |
| Repeated comment text | An anchor for `checkleft run`, disambiguated by context, reaches only the Alpha section; actual attributed output highlights exactly one chunk. |
| Cross-heading comment | A quote constructed across the projection boundary is assigned to both overlapping chunks, and both parsed outputs contain highlighting. |
| Whitespace fragment | `isAnchorable` rejects a newline-only fragment. |
| Large-document hosting | The fixture produces 25 chunks and successfully lays out in an `NSHostingView`. |
| Lazy instantiation | The short viewport reports some chunk appearances without broadly instantiating the document. |

The supporting infrastructure is a new optional `MarkdownChunkAppearProbe` environment value. `DocumentStructuredText.onAppear` records chunk indices into a set. The test hosts the view in an `NSWindow`, pumps the run loop until the first appearance or a two-second deadline, and checks the broad count bound. It does not require an exact prefetch count.

There are no build-system changes. Existing find-index and collapsed-section tests remain in place. The new tests do **not** directly measure cache reuse, end-to-end scroll preservation, or a timing improvement.

The PR description reports successful Bazel builds, `BossTestsShard3`, and `checkleft run`. I inspected the code and tests; I did not rerun those commands.
